devdoc.details: ===== why the split (size constraint, must be understood) ===== The original inheritance chain (...->Staking->Farming->FarmingReferral) had runtime bytecode of **30,747 bytes**, exceeding the EIP-170 limit (24,576), so it **could not be deployed** on BSC mainnet. Measured per-layer contribution:   Storage 948 / Admin +1,792 / Staking +14,429 / Farming +7,318 /   FarmingReferral +3,897 / CoreVault body +891 / read-only views 5,434 After splitting by "business module" each contract is well below the limit:   - **CoreVault** (this contract) = Storage->Admin->Referral->Staking + 31 bare-forwarding wrappers   - **CoreVaultLogicFacet** = Storage->Admin->Referral->Farming->FarmingReferral (farming + op dispatch)   - **CoreVaultViewFacet**  = Storage + all read-only views Precondition for the split: **Staking and Farming do not depend on each other** (verified: both depend only on Storage/Admin/Referral).===== why the wrappers are "bare forwarding" (pitfall) ===== The frontend / CoreVaultViewer / tests access via **typed calls** (e.g. `vault.getRefInfo(u)`), so the compiler requires this contract to **declare** these functions -- a fallback alone cannot satisfy compile time. Hence each moved function keeps an **extremely thin wrapper** in this contract: assembly forwards the raw calldata to the facet, then **returns its return data as-is** (skipping abi.decode/encode) -- each is only about 80-100 bytes, and **does not change** the external signature or semantics.

OwnableUnauthorizedAccount(address).details: The caller account is not authorized to perform an operation.

SafeERC20FailedOperation(address).details: An operation with an ERC-20 token failed.

depositBounds().details: Currently effective farming deposit bounds (post-deployment check / frontend display)      Returns: (BNB lower bound, BNB upper bound, USD lower bound, USD upper bound)

donateFistPool(uint256).details: Requirement text: "mining pool source: 1; any external address may inject FIST". Semantics are symmetric to donateOskPool.

donateOskPool(uint256).details: Requirement text: "mining pool source: 1; any external address may inject OSK". Design intent: **no permission gate** -- any address may call it, and the donation goes directly into this contract's balance,           strengthening the redemption capacity of OSK staking rewards. It is not a privilege: the caller can only **give up** assets and has no withdrawal capability. Pitfall: measure by "balance delta" rather than trusting the input parameter -- if the token charges a transfer tax, the input would exceed the actual received amount,       and adding it directly would overstate _totalDonatedA and distort the audit data (same idea as Treasury's baseline sweep). Pitfall: not counted into _totalPoolA -- the latter means "unsettled principal pool (USD denominated)", while a donation is an extra redemption reserve,       and mixing it in would overstate the pool accounting. See the storage comments in CoreVaultStorage.

emergencyWithdraw(address,address,uint25.details: Policy: **no token restriction, full-amount withdrawal allowed**. WARNING: safety boundary (must be understood): CoreVault only holds OSK and FIST, and both **are user staking principal**   (principal of pools A/B + static yield held on exit). So this function is equivalent to "owner can withdraw user principal" --   this is a capability **deliberately granted to a trusted owner** (for testnet recovery / extreme failure rescue),   and production must replace owner with a multisig (Ownable2Step / AccessControl). Pitfall: apply `transientNonReentrant` -- token is an arbitrary address, and a malicious token can reenter during transfer. Pitfall: reject the zero address to avoid an accidental transfer into a black hole.

getSwapPrices().details: Kept in this contract (not moved to a facet): it is a required implementation of `IAccounting`;   relying only on a forwarding wrapper would leave the interface unsatisfied -> this contract becomes abstract and undeployable.

owner().details: Returns the address of the current owner.

renounceOwnership().details: Leaves the contract without owner. It will not be possible to call `onlyOwner` functions. Can only be called by the current owner. NOTE: Renouncing ownership will leave the contract without an owner, thereby disabling any functionality that is only available to the owner.

setAOskFistPair(address).details: Requirement 2.0 L144: the USD price source of FIST = the mainnet FIST/USDT pair (the original aWbnb/bWbnb dual pairs are deprecated).      Since the 3rd generation this contract configures only **three** pairs: OSK/FIST, WBNB/USDT, FIST/USDT.

setNodePoolDistributor(address).details: Source: `node-requirements-doc.txt` section 1, entitlements -- 30% of network-wide static revenue -> four-pool weighting 5/5/10/10.      The 9/21 on-chain deployment has this selector (3b00b729); this function restores it. Pitfall: only owner is allowed; reject address(0) -- if zeroing were allowed, the node leg would be silently disabled with no trace.      At runtime, when not wired the node leg is **silently skipped** (see CoreVaultFarming), so disabling it should go through "not calling" rather than "calling with zero".

stakeA(uint256).details: Fuel fee policy (Requirement 2.0 section 4, staking rule 2 "2% of the staking amount in FIST is injected into the FIST staking mining pool"):      charged at 2% in the **opposite token** (FIST) by USD equivalent, and **deducted additionally from the user's wallet** -- the staking principal is untouched.      Destination: FIST is injected into the FIST staking mining pool on receipt (this contract's bToken balance is that pool's redemption reserve).      Word-for-word consistent with sections 7.1/7.2 of the design doc `docs/02-design/fund-flow-and-implementation-details.md`. Pitfall: a farming position must already exist to count as **having locked the relationship through farming**; checking only the referrer cannot stop the first user from staking directly.       The gate is placed before transferFrom to avoid invalid approvals and transfers (Requirement 2.0 section 5). Pitfall: the principal (OSK) and the fuel (FIST) are **two different tokens**, so two transferFrom calls are needed and the user must approve each separately --       they cannot be merged into one (the old implementation merged them as the same token, the opposite of the requirement policy).

stakeB(uint256).details: Fuel fee policy (**client change on 2026-09-26**): charged at 2% in the **staking token itself** (FIST),      deducted additionally from the user's wallet -- the staking principal is untouched (staking 100 FIST deducts another 2 FIST).      Destination: transfer to treasury -> half of the FIST is swapped to OSK -> remaining FIST + obtained OSK form OSK/FIST LP -> insurance pool.      Policy **differs** from stakeA: stakeA is still charged in the opposite token (FIST), while stakeB is charged in the same token,      so stakeB **needs no oracle conversion** (pure token count × 2%). Pitfall: same gate as stakeA -- validate the referral relationship before pulling funds. Pitfall: principal and fuel are both FIST, merged into a single transferFrom(amount + fee) -- no need for two approvals/two transfers.

transferOwnership(address).details: Transfers ownership of the contract to a new account (`newOwner`). Can only be called by the current owner.
